promise.text: Address safety in the ByWard Market, including a dedicated Neighbourhood Resource Team and a storefront Neighbourhood Operations Centre, working with police and community agencies.

campaign.title: CityNews · October 3, 2022 downtown platform
campaign.locator: For the ByWard Market · dedicated team and storefront centre
campaign.note: Contemporary coverage; no numeric crime-reduction target. Original archived platform not obtained. CCTV, reporting contact and a mental-health task force are additional commitments not fully assessed here.

portal.title: OPS · Crime Map (Year End)
portal.locator: About, General Terms, and source layer Crime Incidents
portal.note: Founded incidents, categorized by most serious violation and report year. Preliminary, revisable and incomplete coverage of crime. OPS warns users not to rely on this data for comparisons over time. The chart is a descriptive view of this snapshot, not a certified trend or safety verdict.

api.title: OPS · public year-end crime layer
api.locator: Neighbourhood = Byward Market; Reported_Year; four selected categories
api.note: 32 grouped counts independently reconcile with 7,893 transient record rows. No duplicate year/category/GO identifiers in that verification. No identifiers or individual locations retained. Query URLs and response hashes in the snapshot. Service root description still mentions 2013–2022; actual layer/app data covers 2018–2025.

boundary.title: OPS · ONS 2017 neighbourhood boundaries
boundary.note: Uses the same neighbourhood definition as the crime-map app, not Ward 12, BMDA district, Lowertown as a whole or the wider CORE zone. Existing neighbourhood field used; no incident-point geofencing or precise-location inference.

core.title: OPS · November 26, 2024 CORE implementation release
core.locator: More Key Achievements · NOC; CORE launch and geography
core.note: Confirms NOC opened June 2024 and CORE launched that month. CORE also covers Rideau Street and Sandy Hill north, a broader geography than this chart. Hotspot percentages and calls-for-service figures are not spliced into neighbourhood annual counts.

licence.title: Open Government Licence · Ontario
licence.locator: Licence linked from OPS crime-map application
licence.note: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Ontario. Ottawa Police Service is the information provider; this independent page is not endorsed by OPS.

limits: Selected police-reported categories are not all crime, perceived safety, calls for service, arrests, charges or convictions.
Reporting practices, police activity, late reports and offence reclassification can change counts. Unreported incidents are absent.
2022 is an election-year reference, mostly before taking office on November 15. 2023 is the first full calendar year of the term. Earlier years include pandemic disruptions.
No 2026 annual result is available in this year-end snapshot. No zero or partial-year extrapolation is inserted.
No population or visitor denominator is applied; counts are not per-person risk. No inference that the mayor or CORE caused a difference.
The original promise contains multiple actions. Only the operations-centre opening is confirmed here; no whole-promise pass/fail score.
